QF.id: IV Introduction to Interest Rate Derivatives_8

question.text: Which approach to risk management involves taking risk with the possibility of profit or loss?

explanation.text: The Logic: Speculation (or trading) means deliberately taking risk, resulting in the possibility of either positive return (profit) or negative return (loss). Unlike hedging which eliminates risk, speculation embraces it. The Trap: Hedging eliminates existing risk and locks in returns. Insurance selectively eliminates negative outcomes while retaining positive ones. Diversification reduces risk per unit return. Cross-Exam Context: The four approaches to risk management (speculation, hedging, insurance, diversification) are foundational concepts tested in Series IV, VIII, and I. Distributor's Pro-Tip: The market needs speculators — they provide liquidity and take the other side of hedgers' trades. Without speculators, hedging costs would be prohibitively high.
